text:
Alex: Heads-up — saw a 20-30% tail latency regression on the 8xA100 cluster when the job crosses a NVLink/PCIe boundary. Happens only with TP=2/PP=1 config and large KV cache warmups. Profiling attached below.

Meena: Can you paste the profiling snapshot? short summary please.

Alex: Summary: mean token time stable, but 95/99 spikes when all-reduce hits a PCIe hop. NCCL timelines show frequent stalls waiting on cross-node rendezvous. KV cache miss rate increases ~3x during those spikes (we think KV prefetch is getting serialized).

Jorge: paste logs? especially nvlink topology and NCCL version.

Alex: nv=nvlink enabled for pairs, but the task graph schedules some ranks to route via PCIe for certain tensor splits. NCCL 2.12.8. Snip from perf:

```
# timeline sample (abridged)
[0.00s] compute chunk 0 (cudaKernelX) - 1.9ms
[0.002s] enqueue allreduce (128MB chunks) - 0.1ms
[0.0021s] waiting (nccl: PCIe hop) - 2.3ms  <-- stall
[0.0044s] resume, memcpy p2p nvlink - 0.6ms
KV-prefetch: miss->blocking memcpy on rank 3
```

Meena: Interesting — kernel selection + chunking looks optimistic for NVLink but doesn't adapt when a PCIe hop appears. That explains the enforced serialization and KV prefetch blocking.

Priya: Did we change batching heuristics recently? I recall a change to prefer larger chunks for throughput.

Alex: Yes, last week's commit 9f3b increased default allreduce chunk_size to 128MB for better throughput on NVLink-dense racks. But in mixed topology that's harmful.

Jorge: Hypothesis: large chunk size + KV cache prefetch hitting the same bus causes head-of-line blocking on PCIe pairs. Solution ideas: topology-aware chunking, async memcpy for KV prefetch, and kernel fallback to smaller chunk when cross-hop detected.

Meena: Also consider switching kernel to ring vs tree depending on hop count. Ring wins on homogenous NVLink mesh; tree or hierarchical allreduce could reduce cross-hops for mixed networks.

Alex: Quick experiment: forced chunk_size=16MB & enabled async prefetch -> 95pct tail drops from +30% to +6% on same workload. Tradeoff: 3% throughput regression but much more stable latency.

infra-bot: Deploy status: canary job started on ded-qa with config: {allreduce.chunk=16MB, kv.prefetch=async, topo.routing=hierarchical} - run id 20240315-canary-7

Priya: Nice. We should add an automatic detection heuristic: at startup gather fabric graph (nvlink adjacency + PCIe hops) and compute an initial chunk plan. If mixing is detected, default to conservative chunking and hierarchical NCCL.

Jorge: Agreed. Implementation notes:
- Add fabric probe in runtime init (fast NCCL/p2p ping).
- Expose per-job override flag `--net-topology-hints=auto|nvlink|mixed|pcie`
- Kernel selection: prefer hierarchical/allreduce fusion when mixed.
- KV cache: make prefetch use cudaMemcpyAsync + stream dedicated to DMA; fall back to synchronous only on devices without P2P.

Meena: Also add perf counters: pct_cross_hop_bytes, avg_allreduce_wait_ms, kv_prefetch_block_ms. Use these for alerting (SLO: avg_wait<1ms, pct_cross_hop_bytes<15% for optimal racks).

Alex: I'll open a PR with the canary changes and the probe + flags. Plan: land probe + metrics first (small), then kernel heuristics, then default flag flip behind rollout.

Alex: Draft PR link: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/1234

Priya: Cool. For rollout: canary 10 jobs -> watch 95/99 tokens + KV-miss histograms -> if <10% regress, slow rollout to 30% clusters.

Meena: Add regression test in perf harness that simulates NVLink/PCIe mixed graph (we should not rely on infra for tests). Use mock topology + nccl-sim stubs to reproduce stalls.

Jorge: I'll sketch the kernel fallback logic. Potential corner: when TP/PP reorder causes additional cross-hop pairs during dynamic sharding; need recompute when schedule changes.

Alex: Thanks — I'll attach the full perf trace to the PR. For now, canary up; monitoring dashboards updated. :thumbsup:

infra-bot: Metric alert suppressed: will notify if 95p token time > 2x baseline for >5m.

Priya: Great job triaging. Follow-ups: 1) PR review 2) Add perf test 3) Flag + rollout doc 4) Postmortem if we hit customer impact.

Alex: On it.
